names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Αθηναγόρας ο Αθηναίος ο Απολογητής», with the rank word and the two bynames left off. The page glosses the name as Αθήνα plus αγορά, the one who gathers the Athenians, the wise speaker.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Άκμασε στα χρόνια των Ρωμαίων αυτοκρατόρων Μάρκου Αυρηλίου (161 - 180 μ.Χ.) και Κομμόδου (180 - 192 μ.Χ.)» — he flourished in the years of Marcus Aurelius and Commodus, the reigns being the page's own. The same page calls him an apologist «του 2ου μ.Χ. αιώνα».

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Αθηναγόρας ο Αθηναίος ο Απολογητής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The corpus keeps no Athenagoras at all; the nearest thing it holds is Aristides of Athens, the other second-century apologist, kept on 13 September, and that is a different man with a different name. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn and no account of a death. Under the name gloss the page also carries the words «Μιλήσιος στρατηγός» — a general of Miletus — which belong to its dictionary note on the name and not to this saint; nothing in the notice makes him a soldier, and no type is taken from it.
